/-!
# Conjecture 7.57

by V. A. Churkin

A set of generators of a finitely generated group $G$ consisting of the least possible
number $d(G)$ of elements is called a *basis of $G$*. Let $r_M(G)$ be the least number of
relations necessary to define $G$ in the basis $M$ and let $r(G)$ be the minimum of the
numbers $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of $G$. It is known that $r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ for
any basis $M$. Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality
becomes equality for some basis $M$?

Here $d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`. For a finite subset $M$ of $G$, "$G$ is defined in $M$ by the
relations $R$" means that $R$ is a set of words in the free group $F(M)$ on $M$ whose normal
closure is the kernel of the canonical homomorphism $F(M) \to G$ sending each generator to
itself, i.e. $G \cong \langle M \mid R \rangle$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relations, i.e. $G \cong \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$
with $R$ a finite subset of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: PresentedGroup, Group.FG, Group.fg_iff_exists_freeGroup_hom_surjective (none expresses finitely many relations).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.57».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a finitely presented group (only PresentedGroup, Group.FG). Defined as ∃ n (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))), Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels).

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relations, i.e. $G \cong \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$
with $R$ a finite subset of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

blocks.code:
noncomputable def relationRank (M : Finset G) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (R : Finset (FreeGroup M))
    (_ : Subgroup.normalClosure (R : Set (FreeGroup M)) =
      (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : M → G)).ker),
    (R.card : ℕ∞)
blocks.docstring:
The least number $r_M(G)$ of relations necessary to define $G$ on the generating set $M$:
the least cardinality of a finite set $R$ of elements of the free group $F(M)$ on $M$ whose
normal closure is the kernel of the canonical homomorphism $F(M) \to G$, $m \mapsto m$;
equivalently, the least $|R|$ such that the natural map $\langle M \mid R \rangle \to G$ is an
isomorphism. This is $\infty$ if $G$ has no finite presentation on the generators $M$, which
cannot happen when $G$ is finitely presented and $M$ generates $G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.normalClosure, MonoidHom.ker, PresentedGroup (no 'minimal number of relators' notion anywhere).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.57».relationRank
justification.why_needed: r_M(G): least number of relators in F(M) whose normal closure is the kernel of the natural map FreeGroup M →* G (FreeGroup.lift Subtype.val). ℕ∞-valued infimum (⊤ if no finite relator set exists) to avoid the sInf ∅ = 0 junk value.

blocks.name: relationRank
blocks.text:
/-- The least number $r_M(G)$ of relations necessary to define $G$ on the generating set $M$:
the least cardinality of a finite set $R$ of elements of the free group $F(M)$ on $M$ whose
normal closure is the kernel of the canonical homomorphism $F(M) \to G$, $m \mapsto m$;
equivalently, the least $|R|$ such that the natural map $\langle M \mid R \rangle \to G$ is an
isomorphism. This is $\infty$ if $G$ has no finite presentation on the generators $M$, which
cannot happen when $G$ is finitely presented and $M$ generates $G$. -/
noncomputable def relationRank (M : Finset G) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (R : Finset (FreeGroup M))
    (_ : Subgroup.normalClosure (R : Set (FreeGroup M)) =
      (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : M → G)).ker),
    (R.card : ℕ∞)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def minRelationRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (M : Finset G) (_ : IsBasis M), relationRank M
blocks.docstring:
The number $r(G)$: the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of the finitely generated group
$G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None; built on the bespoke relationRank and IsBasis.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.57».minRelationRank
justification.why_needed: r(G) = minimum of r_M(G) over all bases M; defined as ⨅ (M : Finset G) (_ : IsBasis M), relationRank M in ℕ∞.

blocks.name: minRelationRank
blocks.text:
/-- The number $r(G)$: the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of the finitely generated group
$G$. -/
noncomputable def minRelationRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (M : Finset G) (_ : IsBasis M), relationRank M

theorem isBasis_empty_unit : IsBasis (∅ : Finset Unit) := by
  refine ⟨Subsingleton.elim _ _, ?_⟩
  simp only [Finset.card_empty]
  exact le_antisymm (Nat.zero_le _) (Group.rank_le (S := ∅) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

theorem kourovka.«7.57».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Group.FG G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G ∧

blocks.docstring:
Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality
$r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ becomes the equality $r_M(G) = d(G) + r(G)$ for some basis $M$?

Here $d(G)$ is the least number of generators of $G$, a basis of $G$ is a generating set with
$d(G)$ elements, $r_M(G)$ is the least number of relations necessary to define $G$ in the basis
$M$, and $r(G)$ is the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of $G$. For a finitely presented
group $G$ all these numbers are finite.

The trivial group is excluded: it has $d(G) = r(G) = r_\varnothing(G) = 0$, so the equality would
hold for it vacuously.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no existence question: ∃ finitely presented G and a basis M (generating set of minimal size d(G)) with r_M(G) = d(G) + r(G), where r_M(G) is the least number of relators (normal generators of the kernel of the free group on M → G) and r(G) = min over bases; the preceding definitions and the 'known' inequality r_M(G) ≤ d(G)+r(G) are background, not questions; the trivial group (d = r = r_M = 0, empty basis) satisfies the equality vacuously, so a faithful formalization should exclude G trivial (i.e. require d(G) ≥ 1) and the statement begins with 'a)' so only part a) is open and gets the lettered slot.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot faithfully with the same mathematical model (Group.rank for d(G); basis = generating Finset of cardinality d(G); r_M(G) = least size of a finite relator set in FreeGroup M whose normal closure is the kernel of the canonical map FreeGroup M →* G; r(G) = min over bases; trivial group excluded; answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G M). c01 was chosen because it uses ℕ∞-valued infima (no reachable sInf ∅ = 0 default), follows the repository's theorem-naming convention kourovka.«7.57».parts.a inside namespace Kourovka.«7.57» (c03–c06 do not), and includes fully proven test lemmas showing the trivial group has d = r = r_∅ = 0, which documents why Nontrivial G is required. Edits: removed c01's non-slot sorry'd textbook theorem for the 'known' inequality; expanded docstrings to note that all quantities are finite for finitely presented G.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.57

by V. A. Churkin

A set of generators of a finitely generated group $G$ consisting of the least possible
number $d(G)$ of elements is called a *basis of $G$*. Let $r_M(G)$ be the least number of
relations necessary to define $G$ in the basis $M$ and let $r(G)$ be the minimum of the
numbers $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of $G$. It is known that $r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ for
any basis $M$. Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality
becomes equality for some basis $M$?

Here $d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`. For a finite subset $M$ of $G$, "$G$ is defined in $M$ by the
relations $R$" means that $R$ is a set of words in the free group $F(M)$ on $M$ whose normal
closure is the kernel of the canonical homomorphism $F(M) \to G$ sending each generator to
itself, i.e. $G \cong \langle M \mid R \rangle$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.57»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relations, i.e. $G \cong \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$
with $R$ a finite subset of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A *basis* of a finitely generated group $G$ is a generating set $M$ of $G$ consisting of the
least possible number $d(G)$ of elements; here $d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`. -/
def IsBasis [Group.FG G] (M : Finset G) : Prop :=
  Subgroup.closure (M : Set G) = ⊤ ∧ M.card = Group.rank G

/-- The least number $r_M(G)$ of relations necessary to define $G$ on the generating set $M$:
the least cardinality of a finite set $R$ of elements of the free group $F(M)$ on $M$ whose
normal closure is the kernel of the canonical homomorphism $F(M) \to G$, $m \mapsto m$;
equivalently, the least $|R|$ such that the natural map $\langle M \mid R \rangle \to G$ is an
isomorphism. This is $\infty$ if $G$ has no finite presentation on the generators $M$, which
cannot happen when $G$ is finitely presented and $M$ generates $G$. -/
noncomputable def relationRank (M : Finset G) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (R : Finset (FreeGroup M))
    (_ : Subgroup.normalClosure (R : Set (FreeGroup M)) =
      (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : M → G)).ker),
    (R.card : ℕ∞)

/-- The number $r(G)$: the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of the finitely generated group
$G$. -/
noncomputable def minRelationRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (M : Finset G) (_ : IsBasis M), relationRank M

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relations is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The empty set is a basis of the trivial group, i.e. $d(1) = 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBasis_empty_unit : IsBasis (∅ : Finset Unit) := by
  refine ⟨Subsingleton.elim _ _, ?_⟩
  simp only [Finset.card_empty]
  exact le_antisymm (Nat.zero_le _) (Group.rank_le (S := ∅) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

/-- The trivial group needs no relations in its empty basis, i.e. $r_\varnothing(1) = 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem relationRank_empty_unit : relationRank (∅ : Finset Unit) = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (zero_le _)
  have : Subgroup.normalClosure ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup (∅ : Finset Unit))) : Set _) =
      (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : (∅ : Finset Unit) → Unit)).ker := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  unfold relationRank
  exact iInf_le_of_le ∅ (iInf_le_of_le this (by simp))

/-- The trivial group has $r(1) = 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem minRelationRank_unit : minRelationRank Unit = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (zero_le _)
  unfold minRelationRank
  exact iInf_le_of_le ∅ (iInf_le_of_le isBasis_empty_unit relationRank_empty_unit.le)

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality
$r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ becomes the equality $r_M(G) = d(G) + r(G)$ for some basis $M$?

Here $d(G)$ is the least number of generators of $G$, a basis of $G$ is a generating set with
$d(G)$ elements, $r_M(G)$ is the least number of relations necessary to define $G$ in the basis
$M$, and $r(G)$ is the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of $G$. For a finitely presented
group $G$ all these numbers are finite.

The trivial group is excluded: it has $d(G) = r(G) = r_\varnothing(G) = 0$, so the equality would
hold for it vacuously.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.57».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Group.FG G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G ∧
      ∃ M : Finset G, IsBasis M ∧ relationRank M = Group.rank G + minRelationRank G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.57»

items: r_M(G) and r(G) are ℕ∞-valued infima rather than ℕ-valued sInf, so that a generating set admitting no finite relator set gives ⊤ instead of the junk value 0. For finitely presented G all these values are finite (every finite generating set of a finitely presented group carries a finite presentation, B. H. Neumann), so the ℕ∞ equality relationRank M = Group.rank G + minRelationRank G is exactly the notebook's equality of natural numbers; the degenerate case ⊤ = ⊤ is unreachable under IsFinitelyPresented G.

The trivial group is excluded with `Nontrivial G` (equivalent to d(G) ≥ 1), following the decomposition notes; the file's test theorems verify that the trivial group indeed has d = r = r_∅ = 0 so the equality would otherwise hold vacuously.
A basis is modelled as a `Finset G` (a set, as in the notebook), not as an indexed family or list; relators are counted as a `Finset (FreeGroup M)` since duplicates never lower the minimum.

'Define G in the basis M' is read as: the normal closure of the relator set equals the kernel of the natural map FreeGroup ↥M →* G sending m ↦ m (equivalently, the natural map ⟨M | R⟩ → G is an isomorphism), not merely that G is abstractly isomorphic to some presented group with |M| generators.

IsFinitelyPresented uses generators indexed by Fin n and a Finset of relators, up to MulEquiv; G is quantified over Type (universe 0), which loses nothing since finitely presented groups are countable and all quantities are isomorphism invariants.
The existential includes a redundant `Group.FG G` witness (needed as an instance for Group.rank); it is implied by IsFinitelyPresented G so it does not restrict the statement.

The 'known' inequality r_M(G) ≤ d(G) + r(G) is included as an extra @[category textbook] theorem (with sorry) for all finitely generated G and bases M; it is background, not a slot, and is true with the ℕ∞ definitions (Tietze-transformation argument; trivially true when r(G) = ⊤).

reviewer_notes: Original statement ambiguities: (1) 'relations' vs 'relators' — counting relations u = v equals counting relators uv⁻¹, so relators as elements of the free group on M are used; (2) a basis is a set (Finset G), as the notebook says 'set of generators'; (3) the trivial group attains r_∅ = d + r = 0 trivially, so Nontrivial G (equivalent to d(G) ≥ 1 for f.g. groups) is imposed as the decomposition table directs, and this is explained in the theorem docstring. Finiteness of r_M(G) for every basis of a finitely presented group is B. H. Neumann's classical theorem; under IsFinitelyPresented G the ℕ∞ equality therefore coincides with the notebook's equality of natural numbers (the ⊤ = ⊤ case is unreachable). The redundant (_ : Group.FG G) binder is needed only to supply the instance for Group.rank and is implied by IsFinitelyPresented G. No candidate omitted the slot; all compiled. The final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning on the slot theorem; the non-slot sorry'd 'known inequality' theorems present in c01/c02/c08 were deliberately not shipped.
